content.title: Phylogeography and current and future potential distribution of Culex tarsalis (Diptera: Culicidae), a mosquito involved in the transmission of West Nile virus.
content.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To assess the genetic diversity, population structure, and current and future potential distribution of Culex tarsalis, a vector of West Nile virus (WNV). MATERIALS AND METHODS: We analyzed 406 mitochondrial COI sequences to estimate genetic diversity (Hd, π), population structure (AMOVA, STRUCTURE, DAPC), and neutrality (Tajima's D). Ecological niche modeling (ENM) was conducted under current and future climate scenarios. RESULTS: A total of 120 haplotypes were identified, with the highest diversity in the United States, suggesting it as the probable origin of the species. Global and regional Tajima's D values were significantly negative, indicating demographic expansion or selection. Three main genetic clusters were identified, corresponding to the United States, Canada, and Mexico. Ecological models projected potential expansion toward arid and temperate zones on several continents under future climate conditions. CONCLUSION: C. tarsalis shows high genetic diversity, structured populations, and a wide climatic tolerance that could favor global spread. Strengthened biosecurity and entomological surveillance at major ports are recommended to prevent its dispersal.
